correctness.rationale: Direct integrating-factor solution gives v(y)=delta exp((y^2-1)/(2epsilon)) and u/v=kappa(y^3-y)/(3epsilon). For 0<y<1 set t=(1-y^2)/epsilon; equality of normalized squared norm 1 is equivalent to kappa=3sqrt((exp(t)-1)/((1-epsilon t)t^2)). Its log second derivative equals -1/(4sinh^2(t/2))+epsilon^2/(1-epsilon t)^2+2/t^2>0; endpoint divergence proves exactly zero, one double, or two interior roots, plus y=1. Positive nonzero second derivative and nonzero kappa derivative ensure a fold; implicit function theorem yields kappa_epsilon/kappa_0=1+t_0 epsilon/2+O(epsilon^2). Independent SciPy root solver checked 5 positive epsilon, all regimes, and the three-return numerical example. No claim about periodic full-state returns or arbitrary norms.

Scalar entry-exit balance predicts only the baseline return.
